text:
Alex: Heads-up — we should lock a timeline for the new config-early-warning flow. want a short sync on what triggers and what console surface we expose.
Mira: +1. do we mean the prefix-cache / quota spike detectors or the config drift alerts?
Alex: both. primary goal: catch bad flag rollouts before quota burn or latency regression. secondary: give SRE a one-click pause.
Sam: for detectors I'd say: (1) token/sec > 2x baseline for 5m, (2) p99 latency increase > 25% for 3m, (3) error rate > 1% absolute. those map to current telemetry.
Jordan: agree on thresholds but we need a safe window to avoid noisy autopause during normal traffic blips. maybe 3 consecutive sampling windows?
Mira: +1 on consecutive windows. also want a buffered metric for prefix-cache warmups — first 10m of a rollout are noisy.
Lexi: UI note: console should show a succinct card: rollout id, active cohort %, metrics sparkline, and a big "Pause rollout" button with confirmation modal.
Alex: good. also add a small "why flagged" line to surface which config keys changed.
Sam: implementation question: do we attach detectors to the config commit backend or to the routing proxies? attaching at proxies gives lower-latency signals but duplicates rules.
Mira: prefer central detector service that subscribes to telemetry and config events. keeps rules single-source and simpler to evolve.
Jordan: ops-bot: can we prototype with an alert that writes a row to the rollout_events table and fires a slack alert to #eng-oncall?
ops-bot: noted. prototype runbook created: rollout_early_warning_v1. Link: https://internal.redwood/proto/rollout_early_warning_v1 :white_check_mark:
Lexi: question on pause semantics — should pause be immediate (stop sending new cohorts) or draining (stop new only but finish in-flight)?
Sam: draining preferred. gives graceful tail. Implementation: flip gate to 0 for new allocations, keep current KV caches until they naturally finish.
Mira: also need an operator override with TTL so someone can force-unpause for emergency fixes. TTL should default to 30m.
Alex: ops checklist: 1) detectors + thresholds, 2) pause API, 3) console card + confirmation, 4) slack + runbook links, 5) telemetry tags for rollout_id and config_commit.
Jordan: timeline proposal: prototype detectors + slack alert by EOD Wed, pause API + toggle by next Mon, console card later that sprint.
Mira: I'll own detector rules. Sam can own pause API. Lexi can mock console card. Jordan will do runbook and oncall wiring.
Sam: quick API snippet for pause call we discussed: `POST /api/v1/rollouts/{id}/pause` body { "mode": "drain", "reason": "ops-pause" }
Mira: for telemetry tagging: include `rollout.id`, `rollout.commit`, `rollout.cohort_pct`, `trigger.reason`.
Alex: can we add an early warning "dry run" flag so we only alert in a non-blocking channel for the first day? want to avoid alarming product teams.
Jordan: yes — add `alert_level` enum: `quiet` -> slack #eng-platform, `normal` -> #eng-oncall, `paged` -> oncall pager. default `quiet` for first 24h of any new detector version.
Lexi: UX microcopy: confirmation modal should say: "Pausing will stop allocating new traffic to this rollout. In-flight requests will finish. Proceed?" and show links to runbook.
Sam: test plan: shadow pause API (no-op) for 48h, then enable drain mode in staging, run simulated spike job to validate.
Mira: will add gating condition to only enable autopause for rollouts > 1% cohort (avoid small canaries).
Alex: thanks team. meeting? 15m async check-in at 11:15am. ping @Mira @Sam @Lexi if blockers. :thumbsup:
